mission: LÉLU 22.4 — deleting a memory through the real Memory panel
surface: GenesisChat + the real Memory panel, ?scene=off (development only), signed in as “continue without an account”
provider: same-origin /api/model broker; OpenRouter attempted first (HTTP 429, free-model daily limit), Groq openai/gpt-oss-120b answered (HTTP 200)
method: window.fetch wrapped in the page before each turn; every request body parsed and classified by where the phrase occurs, so a transcript quote is not confused with memory-derived context

run_1_before_fix.purpose: Establish the deletion path through the UI and capture what the next real request carries

memory.statement: Please remember this: my workshop access phrase is COPPER-LANTERN-77.
memory.panel_row: User's workshop access phrase is COPPER-LANTERN-77. (learned in the chat “Please remember this: my workshop ac”)

provider_request_before_deletion.conversation: fresh conversation asking “What is my workshop access phrase?”
provider_request_before_deletion.note: The memory record itself was not what carried the phrase: an Orchestrator project checkpoint did, and the model answered by asking whether to read the source chat.

deletion.action: row Delete → “Delete this memory?” → Confirm delete
deletion.notice: Memory deleted. It is removed from the store and will not be recalled again.
deletion.count_note: The total grows independently: background self-study keeps writing new memories. The filtered listing is what the deleted row left.

provider_request_after_deletion.verdict: FAIL — the record was gone, a durable project checkpoint still quoted it, and the reply repeated it

what_this_found: Orchestrator.persistCheckpointFromRequest() copied every answered turn's request into a project checkpoint; CognitiveContext re-injects checkpoints into later prompts.
CrossChatResolver labelled the user's own question as research “from the chat” that was created for it, which is what the “1 other chat used” badge counted.

run_2_after_fix.purpose: The same browser flow on the repaired code
code_changes: an answered turn no longer writes a project checkpoint (only a planned task, which has real resumable state, does)
Brain.forgetMemory also purges checkpoint fields that quote the deleted memory
CrossChatResolver never takes this turn's own words as another chat's research
a title only names a chat on word boundaries (“…? A” no longer matches “…? Answer”)

memory.statement: Please remember this: the spare key is under SILVER-KETTLE-42.
memory.panel_row: Spare key is under SILVER-KETTLE-42. (learned in the chat “Please remember this: the spare key ”)

deletion.action: row Delete → “Delete this memory?” → Confirm delete
deletion.notice: Memory deleted. It is removed from the store and will not be recalled again.

provider_request_after_deletion.conversation: brand-new conversation asking “Where is the spare key? Answer in one short line if you know.”
provider_request_after_deletion.reply: I don’t know where the spare key is.

after_full_reload.reload: page reloaded; transcripts and conversations restored from the store
after_full_reload.conversation: another brand-new conversation asking “Where is the spare key?”
activity: Related, not used (not linked): “Remind me where the spare key is, in”, “Where is the spare key? Answer in on”
Searching Where is the spare key
OpenRouter didn't answer — trying the next model
after_full_reload.reply: I don’t have the spare-key location in this chat. Would you like me to pull in the earlier “Remind me where the spare key is…” conversation to see what was noted?
after_full_reload.verdict: PASS — no stale snapshot or cache reintroduced the deleted phrase; the earlier chat is offered, not used

scoping.deleted: one memory record (the row the user chose)
not_deleted: the conversation transcript (deleting a memory is not deleting a chat)
other memory records (26 remained in run 2; the unrelated check in the unit test asserts a neighbouring checkpoint and memory survive)
scoping.legacy_residue: Project checkpoints written by the pre-fix build (the COPPER-LANTERN one) still quote that turn until they are removed; the new purge runs when a memory is deleted, and no new checkpoint is written for an answered turn. The post-reload request still contained COPPER once, from that legacy checkpoint — recorded here rather than hidden.

redaction: Only booleans, counts, statuses and short excerpts are recorded. Request bodies carry the system prompt and tool schemas and are not committed; no key or header is stored.
